Nina made a wall around a square area, using 36 identical cubes. A section of the wall is shown in the picture. How many cubes will she now need to completely fill the square area.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Nina made a wall around a square area, using 36 identical cubes. A section of the wall is shown in the picture. How many cubes will she now need to completely fill the square area?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The image shows a section of a low wall made from identical cubes, with the cubes arranged in a single layer, and the width of the wall looks like 1 cube; this section of wall is only part of the boundary surrounding some empty square area. Then reason: Let the side length of the square area that needs to be filled be n cubes. Because the wall thickness is 1 cube, the side length of the outer square including the wall is n+2. The number of cubes in the wall equals the outer square area minus the inner square area, that is, (n+2)^2 - n^2 = 4n + 4. The problem says the wall used 36 cubes in total, so 4n + 4 = 36, giving 4n = 32, n = 8. The square area to be filled is 8 × 8, so 64 cubes are needed.

method.method_draft: First describe the picture: the shown wall section is made from identical unit cubes arranged in a single layer, one cube wide, forming the border around an empty square region. From the text, the whole wall around the square uses 36 cubes. Let the square area to be filled have side length n cubes. Then the surrounding one-cube-thick wall would make an outer square of side n+2, so the number of wall cubes is (n+2)^2 - n^2 = 4n+4. Set 4n+4 = 36, giving n = 8. The square area to fill is therefore 8 by 8, so Nina needs 64 cubes.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct perimeter-ring method: model the wall as the difference between an outer square of cubes and the inner square area. It uses the visual cue that the wall is one cube thick and one cube high, plus the text total of 36 wall cubes.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read that the cubes form a one-cube-wide boundary around a square area, with no stacking beyond one cube high; the section shown indicates a border/ring structure made of unit cubes.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the given total number of wall cubes, 36, and the question asking how many cubes are needed to fill the square area inside the wall.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply the formula for a one-cube-thick square border: wall cubes = (inner side + 2)^2 - inner side^2 = 4n + 4, then compute the inner square area n^2.
